About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Uganda program, founded in 2014, provides more than 34,000 farmers with quality farm supplies as well as fruit trees like avocados. Our team in Uganda is headquartered in Jinja, close to the districts we serve, and supported by a small presence in Kampala. One Acre Fund works in the eastern region of Uganda, primarily in the districts of Iganga, Jinja, Kamuli, and Buikwe.

About the Role

One Acre Fund is looking for an experienced, results-driven leader to serve as Head of Government Relations and Partnerships (GR/P) in Uganda. This role leads the GR/P department, driving strategic government alignment, maintaining regulatory compliance, and building long-term government and private sector partnerships to scale smallholder farmer impact.

Responsibilities

Department & Team Management

  • Lead and manage the GR/P department, supervising a team of 5+ full-time staff members.
  • Oversee team workload, set performance priorities, and foster career development.
  • Manage departmental budgeting, financial tracking, compliance, and monthly reporting.
  • Serve as a strategic advisor to country leadership and present departmental priorities to the Steering Committee.

Government Alignment & Advocacy

  • Align departmental vision and strategy with macro-environmental trends and overall country program goals.
  • Position One Acre Fund Uganda as a primary technical and strategic partner to key government ministries (e.g., MAAIF, MoWE, MoT, MLGD).
  • Build and sustain long-term bilateral relationships across national, regional, and district-level government bodies.
  • Lead strategic coalitions with development partners, NGOs, and industry groups to champion joint policy advocacy or coalitions for smallholder farmers.

Compliance, Risk & Operations

  • Work cross-functionally to identify and address regulatory opportunities and operational bottlenecks affecting program delivery (e.g input policies, seed/fertilizer procurement, importation clearances)
  • Ensure strict adherence to Ugandan legal codes, non-government compliance frameworks, and government regulations.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with legal, communications, and field operational teams to ensure smooth program execution.

Partnerships and Stakeholder Management

  • Develop and oversee strategies for strategic partnerships, Government champions and other priority stakeholders, including private-sector, development and institutional partners.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen OAF external relationships and access to decision-makers.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • At least 7 years of relevant professional experience, including 3+ years in a senior leadership or management role involving significant Government engagement, stakeholder management and strategic decision-making.
  • Strong people-management skills, with experience developing and coaching high-performing teams.
  • Strong background in program planning, resource allocation, risk mitigation, managing departmental budgets, and financial compliance.
  • Good understanding of Uganda's government structures, legal codes, non-government compliance frameworks, and public sector decision-making processes, with a strong ability to anticipate regulatory shifts and proactively de-risk operations.
  • A fast learner with an open-minded approach, comfortable navigating complex, evolving environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead multi-stakeholder projects end-to-end, defining workplans, managing timelines, coordinating cross-functional teams, and resolving execution bottlenecks.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to map stakeholders, draft policy briefs and memos, lead public advocacy, and engage senior leadership.
  • Keen analytical capability to interpret government policy and align strategy with key national priorities, including the National Development Plan (NDP IV), agricultural policy, climate governance, and decentralized district-level dynamics.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Jinja, Uganda

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Uganda.

Application Deadline

19 February 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.
